ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2018), PRC Company Law (1993, as amended), Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2019), PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 titled Measures for the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Supervision and Administration of Beneficial Owners of Enterprises, effective 1 November 2024; Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (2020 consolidation); relevant UBO register filing duty under SAMR and PBOC joint decree.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan corporate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Companies Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait document verification route: Taiwan notarization by a licensed notary, certification by the Taipei District Court or Taiwan High Court, then verification by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and forwarding to the mainland Provincial Notary Association for verification before acceptance by SAMR. For any non-cross-strait destination, the parallel path is either Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention member) or consular legalization (non-member); these two are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Taiwan corporate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Commercial Registration Information System)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notarial certificate, SEF verification, mainland Provincial Notary Association verification, then accepted by SAMR as evidence of the Taiwan investor's existence and compliance. For use in third countries, apply only the apostille or consular legalization path according to the destination state's treaty membership; never sequence apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the mainland WFOE incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan parent, notarized in Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Board minutes signed by notarized officer's signature, Taiwan notary authentication, SEF verification, mainland Provincial Notary Association verification, then submission to SAMR for UBO and foreign-investment filing. In an Apostille context, use notarization plus apostille; in a non-Apostille state, use notarization plus consular legalization; routes are alternative and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Taiwan corporate parent (current consolidated version)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (approved and stamped company registration file)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait verification route via Taiwan notary, SEF, and mainland Provincial Notary Association; notarized copy must reflect the latest amendments. For overseas submission to a Hague member state, use the apostille process; for non-member states, use consular legalization; no sequence combining apostille and consular legalization is permissible.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan corporate parent and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Settlement bank of the Taiwan parent (Taiwan-licensed bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Stamp and authorized signature authenticated by Taiwan notary, verified by SEF, then verified by mainland Provincial Notary Association; if the reference letter is issued by a mainland bank and used in Taiwan, the authentication is via SEF inward verification; for other destinations, choose either apostille or consular legalization exclusively according to destination treaty status.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening must cover all shareholders, directors, senior managers, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the PBOC Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Typologies, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, PRC terrorist list, and Taiwan's own AML/CFT designated list. Each candidate must receive politically exposed persons (PEP) status assessment using a risk-based model covering foreign, domestic, and international organization PEPs for five years post-office-holding; negative news and adverse regulatory actions must be reviewed for at least five years. Results must be documented in an obsolescence-safe screening report, refreshed whenever ownership or scope changes, and retained for five years after termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Pre-Approval and Advance Clearance Online System via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (GSXT) portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A PRC company name must use simplified Chinese characters and must not consist solely of pinyin, English letters, or Arabic numerals; a foreign-language name may be recorded in the articles of association only after the Chinese name is approved. The statutory four-tier naming structure consists of administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or operating feature + legal form suffix. A Latin-script brand is transliterated into Mandarin pinyin or an accepted Chinese trade name, and the English or Taiwanese-registered brand is permitted only as the parenthetical secondary name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 30 days and may be extended for a further 30 days through the SAMR online portal before expiry, provided no competing approval has lapsed. Upon a written name rejection, the applicant must file an administrative reconsideration with the same-level Administration for Market Regulation or its superior within 60 days, attaching the rejection notice, the intended four-tier name, and the supporting trademark/BIT registration evidence. The SAMR must respond within 60 working days; if the rejection is upheld, the aggrieved party may institute an administrative lawsuit in a competent people's court within six months. In parallel, counsel should submit a new reservation with a modified distinctive token to preserve the transaction timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaging in programmatic real-time ad exchange and SSP services, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not a safe substitute for a physical registered office. Mainland SAMR registries generally tolerate a service address, but municipal taxation bureaus and criminal compliance units regard a mailbox-only address as indicia of sham operations for cross-border digital advertising income, SWIFT wires, and ACH direct deposits. incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (as codified in the Company Act), administered by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, particularly Articles 1, 2, 18, 99, 100, 101, 108, 113, 128, 129, 154, 156, 161, 172, 202, 208, 237, 274, 387, and 393; read together with Article 73 of the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, the Regulations Governing Permission for Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area People, and the Regulations Governing Fees for Company Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commerce Development Administration (formerly Department of Commerce), Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, acting through the Company and Commerce Registration One-Stop Service Portal; Mainland Area investment approval is issued by the Investment Commission / Investment Administration, MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form (Company Registration Statement), filed together with the Mainland Area Investment Permission Certificate, statutory Articles of Incorporation, Capital Verification Report, and First Board Resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for a Taiwan limited company; no statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed for a digital advertising technology holding or operational vehicle, but the subscribed capital must be fully remitted to a temporary corporate bank account in Taiwan before incorporation, attested by a certified public accountant in a Capital Verification Report, and may not be used for non-pre-incorporation purposes until registration. No government-blocked escrow account is required; the funds are released to the Company after the registration certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED COMPANY (TAIWAN), ADOPTED IN WRITING BY THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER ON [DATE]. WHEREAS, [INVESTOR], a company organized under the laws of the People's Republic of China, has obtained the approval of the Investment Commission / Investment Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, to invest in and incorporate a wholly foreign-owned limited company in Taiwan; and WHEREAS, the sole shareholder desires to subscribe for the entire issued capital of the Company and to fix the corporate governance framework required for incorporation; NOW, THEREFORE,

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan), acting through the Taipei, Northern Area, Central Area, Southern Area and Kaohsiung Area National Taxation Bureaus; online tax execution is handled through the Ministry of Finance e-Tax Portal and the e-Invoice Integrated Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Determine whether the PRC WFOE has a Taiwan fixed place of business or is a non-resident cross-border electronic-service supplier. Step 2 - For a Taiwan branch or subsidiary, first obtain the required corporate and foreign-investment approval and company registration from the Ministry of Economic Affairs, which issues the national unified tax number; the business tax registration then proceeds with the National Taxation Bureau serving the registered address. Step 3 - File the business tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau by presenting the foreign-company certificate of incorporation, articles of association, investment approval where required for mainland-registered investors, lease or desk-use evidence, identity documents of the Taiwan responsible person, and a power of attorney if a local tax agent is appointed. Step 4 - The National Taxation Bureau verifies the submission and issues the formal Business Tax Registration Certificate. Step 5 - For a PRC WFOE supplying digital advertising platform, DSP and SSP services into Taiwan from outside Taiwan without a fixed place of business, the simplified cross-border electronic-services registration channel of the Ministry of Finance applies once annual sales to Taiwan individuals exceed the statutory threshold; the WFOE submits its foreign registration certificate, service description, expected sales volume and local representative details, and receives a VAT/TIN registration number for quarterly Business Tax filing and electronic uniform invoice issuance. Step 6 - If only Taiwan-source payments subject to withholding tax arise and no VAT registration duty exists, a non-resident tax identification number is obtained through the payer's National Taxation Bureau at the time of withholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; entity classification follows the Company Act and tax law. A Taiwan-incorporated subsidiary is taxed as a resident profit-seeking enterprise on worldwide income, while a branch of a PRC WFOE is taxed as a non-resident profit-seeking enterprise on Taiwan-source income without any elective pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (VAT) under the Taiwan Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$480,000 per year of Taiwan-individual sales for a non-resident supplier of cross-border electronic services including programmatic advertising DSP and SSP fees; zero monetary threshold for a Taiwan fixed-place operation, which must register before commencing taxable business. Domestic small-scale businesses with monthly taxable sales below NT$200,000 may qualify for the simplified tax levy.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A registered Taiwan seller must issue Uniform Invoices for taxable sales. Where the electronic uniform invoice regime applies, invoice data including seller tax number, buyer tax number, invoice number, random code, issuance date and amount must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Integrated Service Platform through the approved API or bulk-file channel within 48 hours of issuance or the applicable authorised upload window. The platform automatically reconciles e-invoice data against the Business Tax return and uses the public random code for the uniform-invoice lottery, which serves as the anti-fraud verification mechanism. Designated high-volume digital-platform and e-commerce taxpayers are mandated to issue e-invoices, and a paper or non-registered invoice cannot support VAT zero-rating or input tax refund where the e-invoice transmission requirement is breached.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Business Tax Act, goods physically exported from Taiwan and services supplied from Taiwan to a foreign enterprise or individual for use outside Taiwan, including programmatic advertising, demand-side platform and supply-side platform auction services, are eligible for the 0% VAT rate. The taxpayer must establish that the counter-party is non-resident, the consideration is received in convertible foreign exchange, and the actual benefit or use of the service takes place outside Taiwan; for digital ad services the evidence includes contract terms, geo-location, server data, campaign targeting logs and audience-use records. Zero-rated sales entitle the exporter to a refund of input VAT attributable to those export sales, paid after the National Taxation Bureau verifies the export documentation, foreign-exchange receipt and Business Tax return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued by Taiwan Customs at clearance
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill proving physical movement of goods out of the Taiwan customs territory
Bank Foreign Exchange Receipt or inward-remittance export-proceeds settlement record proving collection of the export price in foreign currency within the statutory period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau cross-checks zero-rated export returns against the Customs export database, the Central Bank foreign-exchange reporting system and bank remittance records. If zero-rating is claimed without the export declaration, without matching foreign-exchange proceeds, with forged invoices, or where the customer or service is later determined to be domestic, the zero-rating is reversed, the 5% VAT is reassessed, arrears interest is imposed, and Article 51 of the Business Tax Act penalty of one to five times the evaded tax may apply. Criminal liability under the Tax Collection Act may be pursued for directors or responsible persons involved in fraudulent invoices, false customs declarations or fictitious export arrangements, and any input credit or VAT refund obtained through the challenged zero-rating will be clawed back.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC, 中国人民银行) as the monetary and payment-system authority; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, 国家外汇管理局) as the delegated foreign-exchange regulator. SAFE administers current and capital account convertibility, bank-led FX registrations, and cross-border payment supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is fully convertible on current account (goods, services, ordinary remittances) subject to authenticity review by domestic banks; capital account items (FDI equity injection, external debt, dividend remittances) require SAFE registration or bank-led recordal, with fund use restricted by the Foreign Investment Negative List and PBOC macro-prudential rules. Taiwan investors in a PRC WFOE are treated as non-resident foreign investors for SAFE purposes. Profit remittance is freely permitted after annual statutory audit, income tax settlement, dividend withholding tax payment (10% standard; limited relief under the 2015 Cross-Strait Tax Cooperation Agreement), and supporting resolution and financial statements verified by the remitting bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory repatriation of current-account export and service proceeds to a licensed PRC bank; since 2012 there is no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio, and FX proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency settlement accounts or converted at the enterprise's discretion. Goods-trade export receipts must be collected within the contractual term; banks monitor outflow/inflow against the 90-day benchmark under the trade-verification framework, extendable to 210 days in justified cases. Service-trade proceeds of the ad-tech DSP/SSP (programmatic platform fees, ad-inventory resale) are governed by the 2013 Service Trade FX Guidelines: full repatriation without a fixed statutory window, with banks performing authenticity checks using contracts, invoices, delivery logs and tax certificates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Currenxie, Global Reach, MultiPass) cannot act as the WFOE's primary settlement or capital-escrow bank: SAFE requires service-export receipts to be repatriated to a PRC-regulated bank account, and FDI equity injection must be booked through a bank holding SAFE-delegated FX registration authority. EMIs are viable only as auxiliary foreign-side disbursement rails (e.g., funding a Taiwan or Singapore wallet for ad-publisher payouts), never as the apex treasury account; any such use must not create gaps in the onshore repatriation trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative and at least one beneficial-controller or authorised signatory must generally attend a physical KYC interview at the opening bank branch under PBOC customer identification rules. Full-remote opening is not available for a foreign-invested WFOE's first account; once the corporate relationship exists, subsequent accounts may be opened via bank digital channels. Taiwan-based directors may use a notarised power of attorney plus Taiwan Passport or Residence Permit and an overseas bank reference, but the first-signatory branch interview is effectively mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: multi-tier Taiwan holding company above the PRC WFOE with nominee-appearing shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group org chart traced to natural persons; Taiwan company registry extract and updated shareholders ledger; notarised certificates of incorporation; written UBO declaration for each 25%+ natural-person holder; source-of-wealth statements for all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ad-tech business abstractness: no physical goods, digital-only revenue, high cross-border payment velocity, risk of round-tripping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed DSP/SSP master agreements; programmatic ad-server logs and SSP auction-flow evidence; invoice and settlement statements matching counterparty-level flows; platform anti-fraud policy; monthly reconciliation of ad inventory bought versus sold; audited financials projecting gross versus net revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection mismatch: registered capital materially exceeds operating burn or is injected in uneven tranches
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan and 3-year budget; foreign-invested enterprise recordal certificate and business licence; SAFE-bank FDI registration confirmation; Taiwan bank remittance instructions aligned to approved capital schedule; step-wise utilisation ledger; negative-list compliance statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP hit, or cross-strait name-screening alerts on directors or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results against PBOC, OFAC, EU, UN and Chinese sanctions lists; negative-hit letters for all UBOs and directors; attestation that no blocked party appears in the payment chain; contractual embargo clauses for all ad publishers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inflow-outflow velocity typical of laundering through digital-ad inventory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy with defined settlement terms (net-30/60); per-transaction economic substance file (contract plus invoice plus service-delivery evidence plus FX purpose code); tax withholding clearance certificates; internal audit trail per payment rail; quarterly reconciliation of capital-account inflows to operational outflows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: (1) complete foreign-invested enterprise establishment recordal and obtain business licence; (2) open the WFOE's Capital FX/RMB Account with a SAFE-delegated PRC bank; (3) Taiwan shareholder remits equity via SWIFT MT103, purpose code 622013 (FDI investment capital) for FX, or via cross-border RMB payment (CNAPS) marked as paid-in capital; (4) bank pre-verifies SAFE FDI registration and performs authenticity check; (5) received funds are converted and placed into the RMB capital-payment-pending account, usable only for genuine operating expenditure and prohibited from equity investment, entrusted loans, wealth-management or real-estate purchases on the negative list; (6) each disbursement is supported by invoices and bank-payment orders and remains available for SAFE non-site inspection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 customer transfer for service-trade payments to overseas SSP/DSP partners, ad exchanges and publisher inventory, with purpose codes per the SAFE current-account classification. Documentary commercial L/C is not appropriate for programmatic ad services (no physical goods); where a settlement guarantee is requested, banks issue standby L/C or performance guarantees. Domestic PRC publisher payouts use CNAPS/HVPS bulk ACH transfers; cross-strait flows to Taiwan publishers may settle in TWD via the Bank of China Taipei branch RMB clearing line or in USD via MT103. All outbound payments require contract, invoice, service-delivery log and, where applicable, PRC withholding tax certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward (远期结售汇) with real-demand documentation for service-export receipts
Onshore FX swap (外汇掉期) for short-term rolling liquidity reset
Onshore vanilla FX option (外汇期权) for purchased protection on forecast USD ad-inventory flows
Cross-border RMB settlement (跨境人民币结算) to structurally eliminate conversion exposure
Offshore CNH NDF or CNH swap executed by the Taiwan parent as a natural offset to the WFOE's RMB expense and USD revenue mix
Currency swap under the PBOC/SAFE macro-prudential hedging framework for long-dated multi-year SSP inventory purchase commitments

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on taxable profit; a 5% additional tax generally applies to current-year earnings not distributed by the statutory deadline.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan has no sector-specific corporate income tax holiday generally applicable to programmatic advertising, DSP, or SSP platforms. Qualifying research and development expenditure may receive an investment tax credit under applicable statutes, subject to approval, eligible expenditure rules, caps, and non-duplication restrictions. Qualifying enterprises may also access separately legislated investment incentives for designated industries or technology activities. Dividends paid to a nonresident shareholder are generally subject to 21% withholding tax, subject to applicable treaty or statutory relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書), filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance income tax e-filing and payment system. The company must use its Taiwan business administration and tax identification numbers and maintain electronic filing records.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a provisional income tax filing generally required in September for qualifying companies unless an applicable exemption applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the annual return and payment are generally due by the end of May following the close of the taxable year. A taxpayer with a non-calendar fiscal year generally files within five months after fiscal year-end. The provisional return is generally filed during the statutory September filing period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taiwan uniform business number, legal name, registered address, accounting currency, fiscal-year start and end dates, filing status, and responsible person.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan-incorporated company is a resident profit-seeking enterprise for Taiwan income tax purposes. Report the Taiwan entity's own identification details; do not substitute the foreign shareholder's tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report advertising platform fees, exchange fees, service fees, data or technology fees, rebates, and other operating revenue on an accrual basis, reconciled to the audited or statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate gross billings, agency collections, pass-through media spend, and the entity's own commission or service revenue. The reported model must agree with contracts, invoices, platform records, and transfer-pricing analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of revenue and operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report directly attributable traffic acquisition costs, media inventory costs, cloud infrastructure, personnel, depreciation, software, professional fees, marketing, and other deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign related-party charges require arm's-length support, beneficiary evidence, service deliverables, withholding-tax review, and proper Taiwan-source income analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report interest, foreign-exchange gains or losses, investment income, disposal gains or losses, penalties, and other non-operating items separately from operating profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify Taiwan-source and foreign-source components separately and review whether foreign income is eligible for a Taiwan foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile book profit to taxable income for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, entertainment expenses, donations, tax-exempt income, deferred tax items, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Book treatment does not determine deductibility. Retain contemporaneous evidence for each cross-border expense and exclude accounting provisions lacking statutory deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable income after statutory adjustments and apply eligible prior-year losses. Loss carryforward generally requires timely filing and qualifying accounting records or certification under Taiwan rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not use losses of a foreign parent, affiliate, branch, or unrelated Taiwan entity. Verify continuity, documentation, and the statutory conditions for each loss year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 20% rate to taxable income, calculate minimum-tax requirements where applicable, and determine regular tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check the alternative minimum tax regime for qualifying tax-exempt income, incentive deductions, or credits; the minimum tax may restrict the benefit of preferential items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim provisional income tax, withholding tax, approved investment tax credits, and eligible foreign tax credits with supporting certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require proof of foreign tax payment, identification of the related foreign income, and compliance with Taiwan limitation rules. Unverified foreign tax cannot be claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report final tax payable or refund, offset prior payments and credits, and complete electronic payment or refund-account information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a Taiwan-designated bank account and reconcile the final amount to the general ledger, tax payment records, and withholding certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepare the separate calculation for current-year earnings retained after statutory adjustments and determine the additional 5% tax, subject to permitted distributions and statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Board-approved dividends, capital reductions, and qualifying distributions must be legally completed and documented within the relevant statutory period to affect the calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose related parties, controlled transactions, transaction amounts, pricing methods, and required supporting schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include foreign parent, sister companies, platform affiliates, service companies, IP owners, treasury entities, and entities under common control. Reconcile disclosures to the Local File and audited accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report payments subject to Taiwan withholding, including dividends, interest, royalties, professional services, and other Taiwan-source payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine whether the payment is Taiwan-source, identify the beneficial owner, obtain treaty documentation before applying a reduced rate, and remit withheld tax within the statutory period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a surcharge based on tax payable, commonly 10% subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts. Failure to file after the relevant notice may result in a higher surcharge, assessment by the tax authority, denial of loss carryforwards, and compulsory collection. Tax arrears accrue interest at the legally prescribed rate, calculated under Taiwan tax rules; there is no universal fixed daily surcharge applicable to every filing default. False reporting, omission, underpayment, or obstruction may create additional administrative and criminal exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a nonresident shareholder. Taiwan resident companies generally receive dividends under a separate imputation and corporate tax treatment. A treaty or applicable statutory exemption may reduce the nonresident rate where conditions are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient, confirm treaty eligibility, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements where relevant, and retain the dividend resolution, shareholding evidence, payment records, and supporting contracts. The Taiwan payer generally applies the reduced rate only when the required documentation and approval or pre-clearance procedure is satisfied. Otherwise, it must withhold at the domestic rate and the recipient may seek a refund or adjustment through the Taiwan tax authority. Taiwan and the People's Republic of China do not operate under a conventional comprehensive income tax treaty; a Chinese parent should not assume treaty relief merely because it is tax resident in mainland China.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Taiwan-source royalties paid to a nonresident are generally subject to 20% withholding tax. Interest paid to a nonresident is generally subject to 20%, with specific statutory categories potentially subject to 15% or other rates. Treaty rates vary by treaty, recipient status, beneficial ownership, instrument, and anti-abuse conditions. Payments for technical, management, advertising, software, data, cloud, or platform services must be characterized separately; royalty or service withholding treatment cannot be selected solely by invoice wording.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Taiwan Local File is generally required where annual net operating revenue reaches at least NT$300,000,000 or annual related-party transaction amounts reach the applicable NT$200,000,000 threshold, subject to transaction-category rules, exemptions, and prescribed documentation requirements. A Master File is generally required for qualifying Taiwanese entities belonging to a multinational group with consolidated group revenue of at least NT$27,000,000,000, subject to applicable conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies at the group threshold prescribed under Taiwan rules, commonly NT$27,000,000,000 equivalent consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not maintain a standalone offshore-jurisdiction Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to the regimes of certain low-tax jurisdictions. Economic substance remains material under Taiwan transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance principle, controlled foreign company rules, beneficial-owner analysis, permanent-establishment analysis, withholding-tax rules, and the tax authority's power to recharacterize transactions. A Taiwan DSP or SSP should evidence local personnel, decision-making, technology and data functions, risk control, customer and supplier management, relevant assets, premises, books, and actual performance of contracted services. A foreign related-party principal cannot be used as a paper allocation mechanism where functions and risks are performed in Taiwan.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of revenue, fabricated expenses, false invoices, omitted Taiwan-source income, manipulated platform settlement records, or deliberate misstatement of taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative assessment of omitted tax, penalties and interest; false or evasive conduct may constitute criminal tax evasion under the Taiwan Tax Collection Act, with imprisonment and fines within the statutory ranges, including potential imprisonment of up to five years and substantial criminal fines depending on the offense and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face criminal prosecution under applicable Tax Collection Act provisions, civil liability to the company and creditors, tax collection against responsible parties where statutory conditions are met, and professional or management disqualification. Travel restrictions may arise from judicial or compulsory-enforcement proceedings; imprisonment depends on conviction and the applicable offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, sham service, or beneficial-ownership abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal Taiwan company with no genuine personnel, functions, assets, or decision-making to route advertising revenue, royalties, interest, or service fees to a foreign affiliate; concealing the real recipient or beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority recharacterization, denial of deductions, withholding-tax reassessment, transfer-pricing adjustment, penalties and interest. Fraudulent structures may also create criminal tax, document, company-law, or money-laundering exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may incur civil damages, restitution, criminal liability for knowingly participating in sham transactions, and enforcement restrictions. Corporate personality is not automatically disregarded, but personal exposure increases where the company is used for fraud, commingling, unlawful distributions, or deliberate creditor prejudice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting DSP or SSP profit through non-arm's-length platform fees, excessive foreign royalties, unsupported management charges, guaranteed losses, non-commercial financing, or selective allocation of valuable marketing technology.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority adjustment to arm's-length income or deductions, additional corporate income tax, withholding-tax reassessment, penalties, interest, documentation penalties, and possible denial of loss utilization. Missing or defective documentation materially increases audit risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face civil liability for losses caused by deliberate mispricing or breach of duties and criminal exposure where false records or tax fraud are established. Mere tax adjustment does not automatically create director imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Permanent establishment and unreported Taiwan business activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A foreign principal operates through Taiwan personnel, dependent agents, servers, sales staff, account managers, or contract negotiators while reporting only a limited local service margin or no Taiwan taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of Taiwan business income, corporate income tax, withholding tax, business tax, penalties, interest, and possible registration or filing enforcement. Contractual labels do not control the factual PE or source-income analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors and responsible persons may face administrative and civil exposure for non-registration or intentional non-filing. Criminal consequences require additional statutory elements such as deliberate evasion, false documents, or obstruction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold or remit tax on dividends, interest, royalties, professional fees, technical services, software, data, or other Taiwan-source payments to nonresidents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed the unwithheld tax, collection surcharge, interest, and penalties and may lose the ability to recover the amount from the recipient. Incorrect treaty-rate application without supporting residence and beneficial-owner evidence is a recurring liability trigger.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face statutory responsible-person liability, civil claims, and criminal exposure for intentional falsification or evasion. Director imprisonment is fact-dependent and is not an automatic consequence of an inadvertent withholding error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register taxable activity, issue government uniform invoices, report taxable sales, apply the correct business-tax treatment, or reconcile gross advertising flows and platform commissions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Business tax assessments, invoice penalties, late-payment interest, suspension or other administrative measures, and possible criminal exposure for fraudulent invoices or deliberate concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may incur civil and administrative liability and criminal liability for knowingly issuing or using false invoices. Personal imprisonment is reserved for conduct satisfying the relevant criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the advertising exchange to layer funds, process circular payments, conceal the source or beneficiary of funds, split transactions, use nominee accounts, or ignore objectively suspicious cross-border payment patterns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential prosecution under Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act and related criminal laws, asset confiscation or forfeiture, fines, account restrictions, and regulatory enforcement. Reporting and customer-due-diligence duties depend on the entity's regulated status and applicable sector rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate, facilitate, direct, or benefit may face criminal imprisonment, fines, confiscation, civil restitution, and judicial travel restrictions. A low-risk AML classification does not eliminate transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit distribution and capital maintenance breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable earnings, disguising shareholder withdrawals as service fees or loans, impairing capital, or repatriating funds without proper corporate approvals and tax clearance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unlawful distributions, shareholder repayment obligations, corporate and tax penalties, possible withholding-tax reassessment, and liability under Taiwan Company Act provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving unlawful distributions may be jointly liable for restitution and company losses and may face disqualification or criminal exposure where the conduct involves fraud, falsified accounts, or other statutory offenses.
